title: The Lawn (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 100bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal life philosophy absurdist garden Perth
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The lawn is the one thing in the garden that requires constant maintenance
And delivers a sense of accomplishment in direct proportion to the patience
You mow it in one direction and then perpendicular for the pattern
And then something in the sky rains heavily and most of the plan's been flattened

[Pre-Chorus]
I have mowed my lawn every fortnight for thirty-seven years
And it's still growing — which confirms a set of fears

[Chorus]
The lawn knows something I don't know
It knows that no matter what you do it's going to grow
The lawn doesn't need your input or your care or your concern
The lawn was here before you and will be here at the turn
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
There's always a patch in the corner that refuses to be uniform
A piece of lawn that has its own interpretation of the norm
I've tried the various remedies — the aeration and the seed
And every spring that corner grows whatever the corner needs

[Bridge]
My father had a lawn in Zimbabwe that was tended by the whole
Family on a Saturday as a kind of household role
I mow mine alone on Sunday mornings before ten
And the lawn accepts this arrangement and keeps growing again

[Outro]
Lawn knows… growing is not the problem… lawn knows
That's my boy
